newsitem.title: USA: IMF to offer Philippines at least $600 mln support.
newsitem.headline: IMF to offer Philippines at least $600 mln support.

text.p: International Monetary Fund support to the Philippines after a currency crisis will comprise $600 million not yet disbursed under an existing loan as well as "additional resources", an IMF spokesperson said on Friday.
The spokesperson said the IMF board was speeding up its consideration of the problem and would be meeting "in the next few days" to consider how to support Manila's economic program.

"The (IMF) board will be meeting in the next few days under accelerated procedures to consider the extension of the current Extended Fund Facility and additional financing in support of the Philippines' economic program," the spokesperson said.
"The amount of IMF finance to be made available will include $600 million that remain undisbursed under the current EFF and additional financial resources to be determined by the executive board."
The Philippine authorities effectively devalued the peso on Friday after massive currency speculation, and the currency tumbled some 11.5 percent.

IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, in a statement released immediately after the news broke, commended the authorities for their "decisive and timely action" and said he would be recommending extending the existing EFF loan and making additional resources available.
